Shares, cash and existing claims

Research cutoff: October 17, 2026. These are explicit analyst scenarios. The original annual forecasts and source records are preserved. Estimates of current balances are not newly reported balance sheets.

The dilution rule

Damodaran normally includes negative future free cash flows and divides equity value by current shares. Those negative flows already charge existing owners for future funding needs. Adding future fundraising shares again would double-count that burden. Completed issues change current cash and shares together. Existing options are separate claims; future stock compensation remains an expense.

Our dated capital controls distinguish reported or estimated current shares, completed financing, existing awards and separately valued option claims. They do not add speculative future financing shares to the same negative-FCFF DCF. Funding access and issuance below intrinsic value remain additional risks.

Damodaran: Share Count Confusion, July 25, 2018 · Course slides, Lesson 5

AAOI: conditional option-inclusive estimate

The unchanged operating path, with an explicit remaining-2026 cash-flow estimate and existing-claim approximation, gives about $40 per share in the reference scenario. This is not an exact security fair value or a live market quote. Edited assumptions and Monte Carlo draws reprice the note and warrant claims.

Estimated October 17 cash: $663.980m
June cash $499.737m + completed ATM net proceeds $587.999986m + estimated elapsed CFO −$42.595109m − estimated elapsed capital spending $381.161741m. H2 cash spending $625m and CFO −$75m are midpoints of an existing analytical envelope. The known property payment and July refund are included once, with the remaining cash movements spread over calendar days.
Remaining economic FCFF: −$281.317m
The October–December stub adjusts estimated cash flow for economic stock compensation, interest expense and interest income. H1 run rates are assumed to repeat; no incremental interest-tax benefit is assumed. The stub and December-origin operating EV are discounted for 75/365.25 years, using 13.5%.
Current-share estimate
August 20 basic common shares 84.906289m + completed ATM shares 5.694845m = 90.601134m. Other unreported changes are assumed zero. The reference additionally assumes all 1.719518m existing restricted/performance awards vest. No future financing shares or future award grants are added.
Existing claims
June bank debt $58.915m and vendor financing $33.940m are carried forward. The note is split into discounted principal/coupons and a conversion option. The full 7.945399m Amazon warrant cap is valued as an option rather than merely at exercise value.
Approximation inputs
80% equity volatility reuses a historical grant assumption; it is not observed current volatility. The October 16 Treasury 10-year 5.09% is a flat rate proxy; the 500bp credit spread is an analyst judgment. The warrant strike uses the original contract's $23.6954; subsequent notes report $23.6956. No extension beyond March 13, 2035 is assumed.

The reference whole-note approximation is $164.796m and warrant value $270.970m. A joint, dilution-adjusted European-call approximation includes time value but omits issuer calls, early-conversion triggers, make-whole terms, averaging, default dependence and path-dependent vesting. This particular joint fixed-point implementation is our approximation, not a formula attributed verbatim to Damodaran.

Volatility assumptions of 60% / 80% / 100% produce roughly $40.52 / $40.15 / $39.85 in the reference case. These are sensitivities, not probabilities or confidence intervals. Using only the initial warrant tranche is another distinct assumption, not verified current vesting.

Nebius: a diagnostic, not a zero-dollar stock valuation

The selected owned-build operating case produces October operating EV of approximately −$11.872bn. Adding estimated cash of $7.895bn and a generous $1.618bn dated private-stake credit still leaves −$2.359bn before any debt or other unresolved claims. Under this particular scenario there is no positive common residual even before those claims. The site must not label this as “NBIS fair value $0.”

Estimated cash and shares
June cash $8.0421bn + August estimated net proceeds $5.680bn + assumed full secured-facility draw $775m − estimated elapsed cash use $6.602142bn. This deliberately generous diagnostic deducts no acquisition consideration, whose amount is undisclosed. Estimated economic shares are June 292.921154m, already including pre-funded warrants, plus approximately 15.8m completed exchange shares. The exchange adds no cash.
Remaining stub
−$4.508748bn: the remaining 75/184 of a modeled H2 economic cash shortfall, with an explicit interest and SBC adjustment. Prior cash use is already in current cash; later cash use is in the operating valuation. Customer advances remain matched to the selected later obligations.
Claims remain unknown
Convertible option values, a discrepancy between old maturity terms and later reported maturity amounts, accrued interest, acquisition terms, employee awards and subsidiary claims need further reconciliation. They remain unknown, not zero. The pre-claim calculation does not need to invent their values.

This is not a conclusion across all possible Nebius business models. A lower-capex sensitivity turns the pre-debt subtotal slightly positive, before potentially substantial senior claims. A partner-owned infrastructure path requires separate revenue-sharing, rental, capacity and replacement-cost assumptions. Higher customer advances must reduce later receipts or create later fulfillment obligations; they cannot be added as free money.

A separate consistency check changes hardware purchase cost together with cohort depreciation and EBIT: operating EV reaches zero at roughly a 20.75% reduction in 2027–2029 purchase costs, or 25.41% if customer advances also fall with spending. A sustained 3.08-percentage-point improvement in operating cash margins also reaches operating EV zero, including matched terminal reinvestment. These are analytical thresholds, not guidance, probabilities, or common-equity values. No source establishes those cost savings or a preferred positive-valued replacement case.

The selected future operating cash deficits are already charged in DCF. They are not added again as current debt or future dilution. The current shares and cash are estimates, not a verified October balance sheet.
